brief: BofA's mid-2025 call (downgrade Communication Services to underweight, upgrade Information Technology to marketweight, on hyperscaler capital intensity, leverage and opacity versus chip/hardware growth) has played out: Info Tech outperformed, and Comm Services de-rated to the 4th percentile in relative forward P/E since 1986. BofA now raises Comm Services to marketweight from underweight because valuations have become more attractive, productivity (real sales per employee) is outpacing the S&P 500 and Info Tech, and AI monetization visibility is improving for Google and Meta, 78% of the sector's weight. Cloud revenue growth is forecast to outpace AI capex growth by 2H 2027, narrowing the monetization gap. Comm Services' 16% long-term growth expectations look more reasonable than Info Tech's record 43%, and high growth expectations have historically correlated with lower subsequent 12-month S&P 500 returns. Debt risk is framed as manageable (Google/Meta debt mostly fixed rate, 17-19 year maturities) though off-balance-sheet commitments are rising over 50% per quarter. Long-only fund overweight positioning in hyperscalers has fallen and is near its lowest since 2023. Separately, BofA raised its S&P 500 year-end target to 7400 and set a new 12-month target of 7800, while flagging the index as expensive on 17 of 20 tracked valuation metrics.

cards.claim: BofA raises Communication Services to marketweight from underweight, citing more attractive valuations, productivity gains, and improving AI monetization visibility.
cards.anchor: raise Communication Services to marketweight from underweight as valuations have become more attractive

cards.claim: Google and Meta together make up 78% of the Communication Services sector weight.
cards.anchor: Google & Meta are 78% of the sector weight

cards.claim: Communication Services has de-rated to near its cheapest relative forward P/E, the 4th percentile since 1986.
cards.anchor: de-rated and now near its cheapest relative forward P/E (4th percentile since 1986)

cards.claim: Cloud revenue growth is forecast to outpace AI capex growth by the second half of 2027, barring another large upward revision to AI capex.
cards.anchor: Cloud revenue growth is forecast to outpace AI spend by 2H 2027, barring another large upward revision to AI capex in 2027

cards.claim: Communication Services' consensus long-term growth expectations are 16%, versus a record 43% for Information Technology.
cards.anchor: growth expectations are far more reasonable (16%) than Tech’s (43%)

cards.claim: Long-term earnings growth expectations for the S&P 500 have been negatively correlated with subsequent 12-month index returns.
cards.anchor: long-term growth rates for the index have been negatively correlated with subsequent (N12m) returns

cards.claim: Meta's and Google's debt is largely fixed rate, with average weighted maturities of 17 to 19 years, at reasonable rates.
cards.anchor: Meta & GOOGL have long-term debt (avg. weighted maturity of 17-19 years) at reasonable rates

cards.claim: Hyperscaler capex as a share of operating cash flow is around 80% currently, still well below the 140% peak reached by Telco.
cards.anchor: Higher capex is still well below peak Telco levels on capex/OCF (80% now vs. 140% at Telco peak)

cards.claim: Hyperscalers' off-balance-sheet commitments are rising more than 50% between quarters, while balance sheet debt is rising more modestly.
cards.anchor: Off balance sheet commitments rising 50%+ between quarters, while balance sheet debt rising more modestly

cards.claim: Long-only funds' relative overweight exposure to Hyperscalers has fallen to 1.22, down from 1.34 in early 2025.
cards.anchor: LOs’ relative exposure to Hyperscalers is at 1.22, down from 1.34 in early 2025

cards.claim: Long-only funds' overweight in Hyperscalers relative to their overweight in Semiconductors is at its lowest level since May 2023.
cards.anchor: LOs’ O/W in Hyperscalers is at its lowest level since May 2023

cards.claim: BofA nudged up its S&P 500 year-end target to 7400, from 7100 previously.
cards.anchor: nudged up our year end target to 7400 (from 7100)

cards.claim: BofA launched a new 12-month S&P 500 target of 7800.
BofA forecasts 33% EPS growth for the S&P 500 in 2026 and 12% in 2027.
cards.anchor: forecasting 33% EPS growth in 2026 and 12% in 2027

cards.claim: BofA's new S&P 500 year-end target implies 3% downside from current levels into year end.
cards.anchor: our new target implies 3% downside into year end

cards.claim: The S&P 500 is statistically expensive on 17 of 20 valuation metrics tracked, the fourth consecutive month at that level.
cards.anchor: is statistically expensive on 17 of 20 metrics (making August the 4th consecutive month the index is expensive on 17/20)

cards.claim: Normalized trailing P/E suggests the S&P 500 will return -3% annualized over the next decade, versus +3% for the equal-weighted index.
cards.anchor: Normalized trailing PE suggests -3% returns per year for the S&P 500 over the next decade but +3% for the equal-wgt. index

cards.claim: BofA sees elevated sell-off risk for the S&P 500 into year end because current multiples imply much lower inflation than is likely to be achieved near-term.
cards.anchor: current multiples imply much lower inflation than we are likely to achieve in the near term, and we see elevated sell-off risk into year end

cards.claim: Higher inflation and long rates are a headwind for longer-duration growth stocks, which make up a large share of the S&P 500.
cards.anchor: higher inflation/long rates are anathema to longer duration growth stocks which make up a decent chunk of the S&P 500
